_comment: The MVP journeys, one entry per complete client or operator path. scripts/mvp-readiness.mjs reads this and scores each journey on three signals: unit coverage of its route files, an E2E spec that walks it, and a production check. `routes` are page patterns and `api` are API route patterns, both in the Next.js syntax that e2e/support/route-manifest.mjs produces from src/app; a pattern that no longer exists is a failure, not a warning, so renaming a route brings you here. `spec` is null when no E2E spec walks the journey yet -- that is the honest state, not a gap to paper over. `tier` is what the journey needs before it can run: 1 keyless, 2 a session, 3 money in Stripe test mode, 4 real infrastructure.

journeys.title: A visitor talks to the intake agent and gets a brief
journeys.status_note: The contract spec posts a minimal valid payload, a payload that fails the schema, and a cross-origin payload the CSRF check refuses. It proves the endpoint's contract, not that a whole conversation reaches a usable brief.

journeys.title: The info agent asks the follow-up questions the brief is missing
journeys.status_note: No E2E spec walks the graph. The sufficiency rules and the graph transitions are unit-tested in src/lib/flowstarter/intake-graph and src/lib/flowstarter/sufficiency.ts; nothing checks them through HTTP.

journeys.title: The pipeline generates a preview site from the brief
journeys.status_note: Generation calls a model through OpenRouter and takes minutes, so it cannot run in a per-pull-request lane. It belongs in the staging full-journey tier, which has no spec yet.

journeys.title: The visitor gets two free edits on the preview
journeys.status_note: The two-edit allowance is a rule in deterministic code, not a prompt. Unit-tested; no E2E spec spends the allowance and checks the third edit is refused.

journeys.title: The visitor pays the deposit and Stripe confirms it
journeys.status_note: The contract spec proves the Stripe webhook refuses an unsigned POST and never 500s, and the production synthetic repeats that against flowstarter.net. Nothing drives a real test-mode checkout end to end.

journeys.title: The payer gets an account against the email they paid with
journeys.status_note: Guest provisioning happens inside the Stripe webhook handler (src/lib/flowstarter/guest-credentials.ts) and forces a password change on first sign-in. Unit-tested; no E2E spec signs in as a freshly provisioned client.

journeys.title: The client claims the workspace their preview became
journeys.status_note: src/lib/flowstarter/claim.ts is the widest-tested module in the journey set. The gap is HTTP: no spec claims a workspace, and none proves a second claim on the same workspace is refused.

journeys.title: The operator watches the build on the board and leaves a note for the agent
journeys.status_note: dashboards.spec.ts opens the board unauthenticated and proves it does not crash. The authenticated half -- a note reaching the agent and coming back in the job log -- has no spec.

journeys.title: The full site is built and published on a real host
journeys.status_note: The production synthetic checks a generated static bundle is reachable on flowstarter.net. A real deploy needs an allocated Hetzner host and the per-host deploy agent, so the full path cannot run in CI today.

journeys.title: The client pays the balance on the final invoice
journeys.status_note: Invoice creation and the portal link are unit-tested against a mocked Stripe. No spec sends an invoice and sees it paid.

journeys.title: The client signs in and finds their project
journeys.status_note: Covered unauthenticated: the client surfaces render and the guard sends a signed-out visitor to login (concierge-flow.spec.ts and contract.spec.ts both check the redirect). Signed in, nothing is checked.

journeys.title: The client makes a small change in the editor and the site rebuilds
journeys.status_note: The size rule that decides rebuild-now versus quote-it lives in src/lib/flowstarter/site-editor.ts and is unit-tested. No spec edits, applies and publishes.

journeys.title: A bigger change is quoted and the client pays for it
journeys.status_note: Quoting and the checkout for a quoted change (src/lib/flowstarter/change-request-checkout.ts) are the newest money path and the least covered. No E2E spec.

journeys.title: The client's own domain serves the site
journeys.status_note: The domains page is checked for not crashing. Verification writes real Cloudflare DNS, so the journey cannot complete in CI; src/lib/hosting/cloudflare.ts carries the unit tests instead.

journeys.title: An operator is invited and lands in the right role
journeys.status_note: The invite page is checked for not crashing. Roles are resolved by resolveUserRole in src/lib/api-auth.ts and proved in unit tests; no spec accepts an invitation.

journeys.title: A client cancels, and money already taken comes back
journeys.status_note: Half built. Cancelling a subscription is a real endpoint. Refunds are NOT built: src/lib/billing/stripe.ts says refunds are handled separately, and src/lib/flowstarter/guest-deposit.ts leaves a failed provisioning loud enough to be refunded by hand. There is no refund endpoint and no refund path in the product.
